entries.name: the fall of the star
entries.summary: A star fell into the land many thousands of years ago, before the town and before the Blood Rot.

entries.name: the Barrow of the Fallen
entries.summary: The Barrow of the Fallen, an ancient burial mound a little outside town: the wealthy town's newer dead on its top floor, a named band of grave robbers within, breaking walls and tombs with the Tomb Sledge to reach the holy relics; joined by a hidden way to the temple's own underground, the Ossuary and the draugr's Hall of Fallen Souls, where the holy knights' relics lie (docs/lore/crypt.md; Jeff 2026-10-27, decision 714).

facts.text: The crypt is a place to keep away from.
The town's first folk moved the old dead down to make room for their own, the oldest as far down as they dared go.
Only the wealthy are laid in the barrow; the poor lie in paupers' graves outside.
The barrow's top floor holds the town's newer dead.
Beneath the temple lies the Ossuary, where the ancient dead were moved, joined to the barrow by a hidden way.
The barrow's third layer, where the oldest dead lie, is damp and dark, too moist for any lamp to burn.
Grave robbers plunder the barrow, and the dead below do not know them from anyone else who comes down.
The dead below are angry at being disturbed, and the draugr's magic moves them.
The draugr keeps the Hall of Fallen Souls, beneath the temple.
Ghostly warriors fill the Hall of Fallen Souls, promised an eternal feast and battle.
The temple's alms go down to the dead, to keep the upper tombs quiet.
The draugr bargains for gold.
Whoever refuses the draugr's bargain must fight him for it.
The door of the Hall of Fallen Souls closes behind whoever enters, and opens again for gold returned or for his defeat.
The Encolpion Amulet encases blessed ashes that protect the wearer, and gives its holder another chance to fight.
Pip carries the temple's offering down to the altar in the barrow.
The Barrow of the Fallen lies a little outside town, under a grass-covered mound with a stone-framed door.
The barrow is an ancient burial mound.
The temple has its own underground, joined to the barrow, and keeps it wherever the temple stands.
The Mound-breakers, the grave robbers in the barrow, have been looking for a way to break through to the holy relics, to sell them on the black market.
The Tomb Sledge, a heavy hammer, is carried by the biggest of the grave robbers; the rest cannot lift it, and the broken walls and smashed tombs in the barrow are its work.
The Mound-breakers stash their take in a chest at their camp in the barrow.
The draugr is angry because the robbers in the barrow dig for the holy relics.
Aldous cannot reach the holy knights' relics beneath the temple, because the draugr has taken up residence there.
A holy knight's remains, returned to Aldous, charge the Encolpion Amulet.
Warriors' spears are planted around the outside of the mound, standing up like spikes.
